pr_body:
The only issue I've found with this PR is alacritty flickers while resizing. I think the content area might be a subsurface, and we don't save or render subsurfaces during transactions. From what I've read in the alacritty project their Wayland support is pretty beta.

My testing includes {floating,tiling} {gedit,alacritty,urxvt} and testing {pointer events,moving,resizing}. Urxvt is included to make sure I didn't break anything with views which use normal borders and no geometry.

Fixes #2178

Fixes #2476

Fairly weird bug:

1. Open Gedit
2. Open the Preferences window, it's a floating window
3. Resize it smaller than the minimum size, it jumps a little at some point
4. Enter and leave the dialog a few times, each time it's configured it jumps and gradually moves towards the bottom-right corner of the screen

Moving the window doesn't fix it.

I can't reproduce that. When I make the preferences window small it stops at a certain size. I don't notice any jumping when resizing, nor when switching focus between the preferences window and the main window behind it.
I still can't reproduce it, even using the default config. Can you try it with the default config if you're not already?
Tried with the default config, same issue.
I can reproduce this too, but it's very inconsistent. Maybe on average once in every 30 times I focus the floating window, it jumps a bit.
Note: willing to file a follow-up ticket for this issue.
Yeah, I'm okay with a follow-up issue as well.

issue_context.title: Window geometry issues
issue_context.body:
Window geometry isn't handled properly.

Alacritty sets a window geometry larger than the surface's size. We don't handle that properly.

Floating windows have an offset on their input region (but no offset on input events).

Should also try to un-maximize tiled views, to check that we handle window geometry for tiled views correctly.
comments:
>Alacritty sets a window geometry larger than the surface's size. We don't handle that properly.

We should report this to Alacritty (and fix the bug on our end too).

>We should report this to Alacritty (and fix the bug on our end too).

No, it's not an Alacritty bug. We just don't support it. They're aware they're doing this.

review_comments: What if the container is not a view and is changing its borders/gaps?

It seems to work as expected. We damage the container (using `desktop_damage_whole_container`) then apply the new state to `current` and call it again. The damage is based off the x/y properties, and these properties are changed when gaps are applied or removed.
